title: Peeling and Chopping an Onion
description: Remove dry outer layers before cutting an onion on a board.
cardDescription: Remove dry outer layers before cutting an onion on a board.
focus: The setting is peeling and Chopping an Onion. Match each clue to a thing, action, or description in that scene.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Remove the outer skin of fruit
Thin flat piece cut from food
Plant part taking up water below ground
Drop of liquid from an eye
One of two equal parts of a measured amount

answerNotes.ONION: An onion bulb has many layers. Its outer dry skin is removed before the inner layers are chopped for cooking.
answerNotes.PEEL: Peel can name an outer covering or the action of removing it. Citrus rind and potato skin are familiar examples.
answerNotes.KNIFE: A knife cuts with a blade. In the kitchen, the board beneath the food supports the ingredient while it is sliced.
answerNotes.SLICE: A slice is a flat cut portion of food. Slice can also be the action of cutting food into those portions.
answerNotes.ROOT: Roots anchor a plant and take up water from the soil. They are below the stem, even when part of a root is visible above ground.
answerNotes.WHITE: White is a color description, not a flower or bird name. Crossings can help when a clue asks for a color rather than a species.
answerNotes.BOWL: A bowl has raised curved sides. That shape helps hold liquid or contain a mixture while it is stirred.

words: Unbaked mixture of flour and liquid
Small sharp fastener used before sewing
Powder ground from grain for baking
Flatten dough by moving a pin over it
Shaped tool used to cut cookie dough
Rounded dish for soup or cereal
Body part with fingers and a thumb
Raised surface where customers are served
Dough used to make a pie shell

answerNotes.DOUGH: Dough is a thick unbaked mixture that can be shaped. A batter is generally loose enough to pour or spoon.
answerNotes.FLOUR: Flour is ground grain used in baking. The fine powder is different from whole kernels even when both come from the same crop.
answerNotes.CRUST: Crust can mean a pie's pastry shell or a loaf's baked outer surface. Both are outer parts, but they are made differently.
answerNotes.BOWL: A bowl has raised curved sides. That shape helps hold liquid or contain a mixture while it is stirred.
answerNotes.HAND: Hand can name a body part or a clock pointer. A clock's minute hand makes a full turn each hour.
answerNotes.COUNTER: A counter is a raised work or serving surface. In a shop it separates the customer area from the worker's space.

subtheme: Whisking Cream in a Chilled Bowl
description: Beat rich dairy liquid until it forms soft peaks.
cardDescription: Beat rich dairy liquid until it forms soft peaks.
focus: The setting is whisking Cream in a Chilled Bowl. Match each clue to a thing, action, or description in that scene.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Open dish with high curved sides
Pointed top formed by whipped cream
Utensil with a small bowl at one end

answerNotes.CREAM: Cream is the rich part of milk. Whipping adds air, which is why whipped cream becomes fluffy.
answerNotes.WHISK: A whisk's loops help mix liquids and beat in air. It works differently from a flat spatula used to lift or turn food.
answerNotes.BOWL: A bowl has raised curved sides. That shape helps hold liquid or contain a mixture while it is stirred.
answerNotes.CHILL: Chill means lower a food's temperature. It does not necessarily mean freeze it solid.
answerNotes.WHITE: White is a color description, not a flower or bird name. Crossings can help when a clue asks for a color rather than a species.
answerNotes.SUGAR: Sugar sweetens baking mixtures and drinks. Granulated sugar and powdered sugar have different textures despite sharing the same sweet ingredient.
answerNotes.SPOON: A spoon has a small bowl at one end. It can hold liquid, unlike the prongs of a fork.
answerNotes.SOFT: Soft describes something that yields to touch. It can refer to cloth, an animal's fur, or food that is easy to bite.

answerNotes.PASTA: Pasta comes in many shapes. Spaghetti is long and thin, while macaroni is commonly sold as short tubes.
answerNotes.WATER: Water is the same liquid whether it is in a drinking glass, a garden hose, or a cooking pot. The container changes the scene, not the substance.
answerNotes.POT: Pot can name a cooking vessel or a plant container. The surrounding clues tell you which everyday use is intended.
answerNotes.HANDLE: A handle is the part made for the hand to grip. Its shape depends on whether the object is carried, pulled, poured, or turned.
answerNotes.HOT: Hot describes temperature. A hot dog is a food name, so the two-word phrase has a meaning beyond the adjective alone.

answerNotes.CHEESE: Cheese comes in many textures and flavors. Sharp describes flavor, while a wedge describes the shape of a cut portion.
answerNotes.BOWL: A bowl has raised curved sides. That shape helps hold liquid or contain a mixture while it is stirred.
answerNotes.HANDLE: A handle is the part made for the hand to grip. Its shape depends on whether the object is carried, pulled, poured, or turned.
answerNotes.METAL: Metal names a family of materials including iron, copper, and aluminum. The word does not identify which metal a particular tool contains.
answerNotes.PLATE: A plate is flatter than a bowl. Its broad surface is useful for separate portions of a meal.
